title: Exact scalar localization, slice restriction and the lisse image
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme, without separatedness [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] set $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $A_X=B_X[1/t]$, the sheafification of sectionwise localization. Use ordinary module sheaves, sheaf tensor products and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,R)$ for the integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $Q_X:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=D^b_c(X,E)$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $F_X:D(B_X)\to D(A_X)$ for $K\mapsto A_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$. Write $J_X(Q_XK)=F_XK$, $J_X(u\otimes a)=aF_X(u)$ for the induced functor. A lisse rational object means an object of the standard heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite sum of coefficient units [def-real-rational-lisse-heart]. A finite locally free module sheaf means one pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_X^{\oplus r}$, allowing rank zero and varying finite ranks.

The functor $F_X$ is induced by exact scalar localization on module sheaves and satisfies $\mathcal H^i(F_XK)\cong A_X\otimes_{B_X}\mathcal H^i(K)$ naturally for every $K\in D(B_X)$ and every integer $i$. It takes the localized standard cohomological halves [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] into the corresponding ambient halves.

For every object $j:U\to X$ of the small pro-etale site, restriction to the slice site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies $B_X|_U=B_U$, $A_X|_U=A_U$ and their finite residue projections and localization units. Under the canonical identification of the slice with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, restriction commutes with sheaf tensor, the strict derived inverse limit used for completed coefficients (total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, with its normalized projections [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], realizing [def-weil-derived-limit]), and $F$: $(F_XK)|_U\cong F_U(K|_U)$ whenever defined. No finite-type hypothesis on the chart $U$ is required. These comparisons send local scalar fractions and tensors to the same fractions and tensors. In particular $J_X$ takes every lisse rational object to a finite locally free $A_X$-module sheaf in degree zero, and the coefficient unit to $A_X[0]$. For lisse $K,L$, the degree-zero identification of $J_XK,J_XL$ identifies their derived Hom set with the Hom set of their ordinary module sheaves.

proof.text: Apply nonempty_localizationData on X and on every chart. Each model is an existential witness only; the ordinary object and map formulas and universal counit fix its comparisons. Obtain each normalized chart comparison with localization_slice. Apply exists_localizedSiteTensorRestriction separately to the integral and rational rings.

A rational lisse heart object belongs to both standard degree-zero halves. The LocalizationData.halves field proves its image IsGE 0 and IsLE 0. Apply Mathlib exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE, then apply H^0 and singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso to identify its single module with its actual H^0. Whiskering the inverse module isomorphism with singleFunctor gives exactly the required degree-zero identification. This is the proved helper heart_image_single.

Apply localization_localFreeness to the chosen models and the assembled slice data. Pair its finite-local-freeness conclusion with the degree-zero identification already proved, and retain its coefficient-unit isomorphism.

Choose the two degree-zero identifications from the proved helper. Mathlib full faithfulness of singleFunctor gives a bijection on ordinary module Homs; compose with Iso.homCongr for the inverse of both identifications. The resulting map is definitionally f ↦ eK.hom ≫ singleFunctor.map f ≫ eL.inv, as stated.

No new nodes and no fixes. Live and side-live still show the item unsplit, so no other group superseded it. There is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. Each step's uses equal proof_deps, all cited ids exist, there is no SGA and no doubled backslash, and a DFS over 11972 dependency nodes finds no cycle back to the item. Statement change, diffed against Q130's base copy: the worker added definition references for the localized ringed site and the sheaf tensor product, and fixed which limit 'the strict derived inverse limit' means (the total right derived limit on strict towers of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit). This makes the clause precise rather than weaker: def-weil-derived-limit alone is only a property of a triangle, not a functor. The only citer, lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization, is unaffected. Source: Bhatt-Scholze 6.8.2 (O_E,X = lim O_E/ϖ^n; E_X = O_E,X[1/ℓ]), 6.8.3 (lisse = locally free of finite rank) and 6.8.14(2) agree with A_X = B_X[1/t], J_X and the finite locally free target. Steps: (1) the per-rational localization lemma's hypotheses hold: B_X has a constant O_E map and C_X is a full O_E-linear triangulated subcategory of D(B_X), with the raw scalar localization. It gives exactness, F ≅ D(T), H^r for all r and the fraction formula. (2) The rational halves are defined through integral representatives, so the heart image has cohomology only in degree 0; the two halves may use different representatives. (3) The slice equivalence, the coherence slice clause with g = id, and localization-restriction with U → X final and f = t give b/t^m ↦ b|_U/t^m from the statement itself. (4) Exact restriction plus the termwise derived factorization plus the pure-tensor-normalized tensor restriction give (F_X K)|_U ≅ F_U(K|_U). (5) The slice strict-derived-limit lemma applies directly. (6) The integral pullback is a derived limit of the finite slice restrictions; the derived tensor pullback identifies the towers naturally, and derived-limit existence clause 1 gives Lj^*H ≅ H|_U objectwise. 'Strict' there is loose wording only; the argument does not depend on it. (7) concentrated-single plus the chart isos plus exact-functor cohomology give M|_U ≅ A_U^r, including rank 0 and varying ranks, and the coefficient unit goes to A_X[0]. (8) derived-single-fully-faithful gives the Hom clause. Edge cases checked: empty X, rank 0, torsion representatives, unbounded and negative degrees, charts not of finite type; no product exactness is assumed anywhere. The split_report tool_uses (nine generic ringed-site and derived-limit lemmas from other units) are accepted.
